inline_comments.comment: This file is an AI assistant instruction prompt that was accidentally committed to the repository root. It contains no production code and should not be tracked in version control. It should be added to `.gitignore` or deleted. The `.instructions/` directory was already added to `.gitignore` in this PR, but the `instructions.md` file itself at the root was not excluded.

This silently changes the default layout for **all existing mindmap diagrams** from `cose-bilkent` to `tidy-tree`. Any user who has a published or embedded mindmap without an explicit `layout:` frontmatter will suddenly get a completely different visual layout after upgrading. The PR description states `cose-bilkent` is the intended default (in the changeset and config schema), yet this code overrides the config here. If the goal is to make `tidy-tree` the mindmap default, it should be done in the config schema/defaults (`config.schema.yaml`) where it is explicit and documented, not as a silent override in preprocessing.

The `validateLayoutData` function requires `data.rootNode`, which is a mindmap-specific concept. However, `cose-bilkent` is now registered as a general-purpose layout algorithm (via `registerDefaultLayoutLoaders` in `render.ts`) and could receive `LayoutData` from any diagram type. Any non-mindmap diagram that selects `cose-bilkent` as its layout will throw `'Root node is required'` even if the graph is otherwise valid. Either rename this to a mindmap-specific validator, move `rootNode` to a required mindmap subtype, or remove the `rootNode` requirement from the general algorithm.

`diagramId: 'mindmap-' + Date.now()` generates a different ID on every call to `getData()`. This causes several problems: (1) calling `getData()` multiple times in a render cycle produces inconsistent IDs; (2) snapshot tests will always fail because the ID changes between runs; (3) the ID is used for DOM element lookups — a changing ID means referencing a stale element. Use a stable identifier derived from the diagram content or passed in as a parameter (the `id` parameter already exists on `draw(text, id, ...)`). The `id` from `draw()` is available in the renderer and should be set on `data4Layout.diagramId` there rather than generated here.

The `this.getType = this.getType.bind(this)` line was removed from the constructor. If `getType` is called as a callback somewhere (e.g., in the grammar or parser that uses the DB), it will lose its `this` context and throw. The other methods (`getMindmap`, `getElementById`, `getParent`, etc.) all have their bindings preserved. Verify that `getType` is never passed as a standalone callback; if it is, restore the binding.

There are now at least 15 elements with `id="diagram4"` in this file. Duplicate `id` attributes are invalid per the HTML spec and cause unpredictable behavior: `document.getElementById('diagram4')` will return only the first element, and Mermaid's own DOM selectors may attach to the wrong element. Each diagram should have a unique `id`. Additionally, this file contains large amounts of development-only test content (e.g., repeated long lorem-ipsum strings in diagram nodes). Consider whether this file is intended to be in the repository at all, or whether these examples belong in a dedicated test fixture.

`let intersectionShift = 50;` is a dead assignment — it is immediately overwritten with `intersectionShift = 30` inside the Promise (line ~55) before it is ever read. Either initialize directly to `30` at the declaration site, or remove the outer declaration and declare it as `const` inside the try block where it is actually set.

`executeTidyTreeLayout` wraps synchronous-ish logic in `new Promise((resolve, reject) => { try { ... } catch (error) { reject(error); } })`. This is the [explicit-Promise-constructor antipattern](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/rules/no-async-promise-executor). The code contains no inherently asynchronous operations (the `Layout.layout()` call is synchronous). Either declare the function as `async` and use `try/await/catch`, or return the result directly. The current approach can also silently swallow errors if the `resolve()` call itself throws.

Multiple debug-level log calls serialize the entire `elkGraph` object using `JSON.stringify(elkGraph, null, 2)`. For complex diagrams, `elkGraph` can be a large object with deeply nested node/edge trees. Even at `debug` level, `JSON.stringify` is called eagerly on every render cycle. Consider guarding these calls with a check like `if (log.level <= 4) { log.debug(...) }`, or simply remove these development-time diagnostics before merging. Similarly, the `APA01`, `APA12`, `APA16`, etc. tracking codes are internal development artefacts that should be cleaned up.

`log.debug('APA01 positionedEdge', positionedEdge)` — the `APA01` prefix appears throughout multiple files in this PR as an internal tracking code. These should be removed or replaced with meaningful log messages before the code is merged. Debug logs that reach production help users diagnose issues, so they should describe what is happening, not reference internal development codes.

The `_drawNodes` function (renamed from `drawNodes` with an underscore prefix indicating it is meant to be private/unused) is never called in the new rendering flow — the unified `render()` system handles node insertion. Similarly, `_updateNodeDimensions` defined on line ~33 is also never called. Both are dead code left over from the refactoring. They should be removed to avoid confusion about the actual rendering pipeline.

`// lineData = fixCorners(lineData);` — the old `fixCorners` function was replaced by `adjustForArrowHeads`, but the commented-out call was left in. Dead comments like this leave readers uncertain whether the line was intentionally disabled or accidentally omitted. Remove it.

The entire function body was wrapped in an extra anonymous block `{ }`. While syntactically valid, this adds an unnecessary level of nesting and is not a JavaScript idiom. It makes the diff harder to read (all lines appear modified) and provides no scoping benefit since `let`/`const` are already block-scoped at the `if` statement level. Revert to the original flat structure — the meaningful changes here (converting `var` to `const`/`let` and using `Math.abs` for the near-zero check) don't require the extra block.

`const loader = async () => await import('./render.js')` — the `async/await` wrapper around `import()` is redundant. Dynamic `import()` already returns a `Promise`, so this is equivalent to `const loader = () => import('./render.js')`. The extra wrapping adds a microtask tick and slightly increases the callstack depth with no benefit.

The alternating split `index % 2 === 0 → left, else → right` distributes root children as: [child0, child2, child4…] → left, [child1, child3, child5…] → right. This interleaves children rather than splitting the list in half. The PR description says odd-indexed go right and even-indexed go left, which matches. However, consider whether this is the best user experience: a mindmap with children `[A, B, C, D]` puts `A, C` on the left and `B, D` on the right, which may surprise users who expect `A, B` left and `C, D` right. A comment explaining the rationale for this specific distribution would help future maintainers.

Both `cloud` and `bang` use `intersect.rect(bounds, point)` for `calcIntersect`, meaning edges will connect to the rectangular bounding box rather than the actual cloud/bang shape boundary. For the tidy-tree layout where `calcIntersect` is used to route edges, this means edges visually pass through the bumpy cloud outline before appearing to terminate. Using `intersect.rect` is the same as the existing `drawRect` shape, defeating the purpose of having distinct shapes. A polygon or ellipse approximation would be more accurate for cloud shapes specifically.

`cytoscape.use(fcose as any)` uses a type assertion to suppress a TypeScript error. Separately, the layout options type was widened from `FcoseLayoutOptions` (which provides compile-time checking for fcose-specific options like `quality`, `nodeRepulsion`, etc.) to the generic `LayoutOptions`. These changes together silently reduce type safety: invalid fcose-specific option names will no longer produce compiler errors. The correct fix is to ensure the `cytoscape-fcose` type definitions are compatible with the installed version, or add a proper ambient declaration.

general_comments.comment: **Inconsistent validation contracts across layout algorithms.** `cose-bilkent/layout.ts` validates `data.rootNode` as required, while `mermaid-layout-tidy-tree/layout.ts` does not. This means the two algorithms that are both registered for mindmap rendering have different preconditions. If a third layout algorithm is added, it is unclear which contract to follow. Consider extracting shared mindmap-specific validation into a common helper (e.g., `validateMindmapLayoutData`) that all mindmap-capable algorithms can call, distinct from the general `validateLayoutData` contract.

**`PositionedEdge` interface does not declare `points`** in `packages/mermaid-layout-tidy-tree/src/types.ts`. The `calculateEdgePositions` function returns objects with a `points: Point[]` field, and `render.ts` accesses `positionedEdge.points` to build the edge path. Because `PositionedEdge` only carries this property via the index signature `[key: string]: unknown`, TypeScript types `positionedEdge.points` as `unknown`. This means the `render.ts` code silently performs an implicit unsafe assignment without any type error. Add `points?: Point[]` explicitly to the `PositionedEdge` interface.

**Large HTML test fixture contains development-only debugging content.** `cypress/platform/knsv2.html` and the new `cypress/platform/mindmap-layouts.html` are appropriate as development scratch pads, but several entries in `knsv2.html` contain very long repeated filler text strings (multiple paragraphs of lorem ipsum in node labels) that are clearly from manual testing. These make the file hard to diff, increase test setup cost, and add little value as permanent test cases. Either move these to dedicated Cypress spec tests, or trim the file to the minimal cases needed.

**`packages/mermaid-layout-tidy-tree/README.md` is missing code fences.** The README contains code examples (`flowchart-tidy-tree TD`, shell commands, TypeScript import blocks, HTML snippets) that are displayed as plain text rather than fenced code blocks. This makes the package documentation hard to read on GitHub and npm. Add triple-backtick fences with appropriate language tags (` ```sh `, ` ```ts `, ` ```html `).
